title: The Alpha Trailer Is Here, and Bobby Deol Names a Baby Sita. YRF Just Reinvented Its Own Spy Universe — With Two Women.
excerpt: Alia Bhatt narrates her own origin story, Sharvari stays a mystery, and the closing seconds confirm the cameo fans were begging for. Alpha hits theatres July 3.
body:
It opens on an image you don't expect from a YRF spy film: an infant, sealed inside a glass enclosure, and a man leaning in to name her. The man is **Bobby Deol**. The name he gives the child is Sita. And just like that, the much-awaited **Alpha** trailer announces it has no interest in playing the genre the way Pathaan and War played it.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0</youtube>

The trailer dropped at midday on June 17, and within hours it was the only thing Bollywood Twitter wanted to argue about. Headlined by **Alia Bhatt** and **Sharvari**, with **Anil Kapoor** and Bobby Deol in pivotal roles, *Alpha* is the YRF Spy Universe's first female-fronted theatrical venture — and the trailer is built to make sure you never forget that detail.


![Bobby Deol — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/01/Lord_Bobby_2024.jpg)



> **"By the time she's grown, she isn't a princess anymore."**



Alia's voiceover takes over almost immediately, narrating the story of a princess as the visuals carry her character from childhood to adulthood. We watch her trained, hardened, sharpened — years of discipline compressed into a montage of bruises and gunmetal. By the time she's grown, she isn't a princess anymore. She's a weapon, and she knows it.

> "The origin story of two deadly girls." — YRF's own framing for *Alpha*

That framing is doing a lot of work, because the trailer is conspicuously stingy with one of its two leads. Sharvari — who turned 30 the week the trailer launched, with Alia posting a public note calling her "a star" — appears in exactly one electric moment: a brief, charged confrontation with Alia that the editors cut away from before you can breathe. The makers have deliberately kept her character under wraps. It's a tease, and it's a smart one. You leave the trailer knowing more about Bobby Deol's villain than about the woman sharing the poster.


![Spy Universe — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/d/d6/YRF_Spy_Universe_logo.jpg)


And what a villain. Deol's character, the one who named the baby Sita, appears to turn against India while running a shadowy program called Alpha. After his quietly terrifying turn in *Animal*, Deol has become Bollywood's most reliable purveyor of menace, and the trailer leans on that hard. Anil Kapoor, meanwhile, plays the other pole — mentoring and guiding Alia's character, hinting at a mission that could reshape the spy universe's future. At 69, Kapoor still walks into a frame and owns it.

The aesthetic is pure YRF maximalism: chase sequences, gun battles, hand-to-hand combat staged across what looks like several continents and a substantial chunk of Aditya Chopra's bank account. Director **Shiv Rawail**, who made the acclaimed *The Railway Men*, shoots Alia's action with a weight and grit that the franchise's male-led entries often skipped in favour of slow-motion swagger. Cranking the adrenaline is global Top DJ **HUGEL**'s worldwide chartbuster "Jamaican Bam Bam," dropped over the cut like a shot of espresso — an unusual, slightly audacious music choice that mostly works.

Then comes the closing-moment surprise the whole campaign was engineered around. The trailer confirms that **Hrithik Roshan**'s Kabir — the RAW agent at the heart of *War* — will make a special appearance in *Alpha*. The reveal stitches this female-led origin story directly into the spine of the universe, and judging by the timeline reactions, it's exactly the validation a section of the audience was waiting for.

Because here's the subtext nobody at YRF is saying out loud: *Alpha* has been a troll magnet for months. A vocal corner of the internet decided to write the film off before a single frame of footage existed — partly reflexive Alia Bhatt skepticism, partly discomfort with a woman carrying an action tentpole this size. The Hrithik cameo is, among other things, a quiet rebuttal. The boys' club is co-signing.

For the diaspora, the date to circle is **July 3, 2026**, when *Alpha* hits theatres worldwide — including a wide North American and UK release through YRF's international network, the same pipeline that turned Pathaan and Jawan into overseas monsters. It arrives the same day as Huma Qureshi's *Baby Do Die Do*, making July 3 an unexpected face-off between two desi female-assassin films.

Is *Alpha* going to be good? The trailer can't promise that. What it promises is scale, a genuinely fresh premise, and two actresses being handed the kind of mythic, blood-and-gunpowder material Bollywood has reserved for its men for the better part of a century. After decades of women as eye candy in these films, watching one narrate her own origin story — princess to predator — feels, frankly, overdue.
